lesson.subtitle: Lesson 8 -- The 3-Minute Update
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Joyce Michalczuk | Lesson 8 -- The 3-Minute Update

listenings.text: I lead financial planning for the group, and I sit through about thirty country updates every quarter. The ones I remember open with the ask. In the first thirty seconds, tell me what you need from this meeting: a decision, money, or just attention. Then give me three points, and tell me when you move from one to the next, so I always know where we are. Your slides are a backup, not a script. If you read them to me, I stop listening, because I can read faster than you can speak. Three minutes, three points, one ask. That is an update I can act on.

I am the chief financial officer for Europe, and I think the three-point update is too fast for a topic like the Brazilian reform. If you open with the ask, I do not yet understand why I should say yes. For me, the first minute is context. A short story: what happened, what changed, why it matters now. Then the number means something, and the ask feels natural. I do not need thirty slides. I need to understand the situation well enough to defend it in front of my own board. Give me the story first. I will give you the decision after.
